biological_support.dimension_interpretation: K7_C0001 (n=14 vs rest n=89) shows a coherent, strongly down-shifted transcriptomic phenotype relative to the rest of the partition, dominated by coordinated suppression of oxidative phosphorylation (NES -2.49), adipogenesis, fatty acid metabolism, estrogen response, xenobiotic metabolism, protein secretion, bile acid metabolism, and related metabolic programs, all at FDR q=0.001. The leading-edge gene sets for these pathways overlap heavily (e.g., mitochondrial OXPHOS and TCA-cycle genes such as PDHA1, FH, SUCLG1, MDH1, NDUFS8, ATP5F1A, COX5A recur across pathways), indicating a shared metabolic program rather than many independent signals. Only a few up-regulated pathways appear, and none reach FDR significance (angiogenesis NES 1.42 q=0.188; E2F targets NES 1.32 q=0.209). The pattern is directionally consistent and interpretable as a distinct metabolic phenotype relative to the rest of the partition.
